headline: Neighbors already know McNeil's. Google just uses a longer name and a later close.
summary: McNeil's Tree Service has been taking care of trees around Lakeside and Santee since 1983, and the neighbors have noticed: the shop was a Nextdoor Neighborhood Favorite in both 2024 and 2025. The phone number is the same everywhere we looked, the website is up with clear services and weekday hours, Yelp and Nextdoor both point people to the same street in Lakeside, and your Google listing is up with the website linked. The one thing that stands out is the Google card. It lists the shop as McNeils Tree Service ISA Certified Arborist and shows weekday hours of 9 to 6, while your website says McNeil's Tree Service and Monday to Friday 9 to 5. Matching the name and the closing time on Google to the site keeps search and callers looking at the same shop. A few smaller things would tidy up behind it: the shop name reads a little differently on Yelp than on your site, and the website talks about Santee while the shop is in Lakeside. None of this is urgent, and all of it is the kind of quiet fix that tends to keep paying off for years.

signals.note: Your Google listing is up as McNeils Tree Service ISA Certified Arborist, marked open, with your website and phone linked. People searching for a tree service can land on you. Neighbors on Nextdoor named you a Neighborhood Favorite in 2024 and 2025, so the word of mouth is there; Google is carrying it under a longer name.
signals.next: In Google Business Profile, set the public name to match the site (McNeil's Tree Service) if you want one name everywhere, and set weekday hours to the same 9 to 5 the site prints, unless 9 to 6 is the real door time.

signals.note: Your number, (619) 884-6303, matches on your website, Nextdoor and Yelp, so anyone who finds you can reach you. That consistency is worth protecting. The Google listing should keep using this exact same number.
signals.next: Keep (619) 884-6303 as the one number everywhere, including Google. If you ever add a second line, list it as additional rather than replacing this one.

signals.note: Your website clearly lists Monday through Friday 9:00am to 5:00pm, closed weekends. Google currently shows 9 to 6 on weekdays. Most people check hours right on Maps before they call.
signals.next: Pick the real weekday close, 5 or 6, and use that same set on the site and on Google. Mark weekends closed on both. If you take storm calls after hours, Google lets you add a short note about that.

signals.note: Tree work sells on before-and-after pictures, and you have over four decades of jobs behind you. The Google listing is live, so there's already a place for crew, truck and finished-work photos.
signals.next: Add 5 to 10 real photos to the profile: the truck and bucket, a removal in progress, a clean yard after a stump grind. Adding a fresh one every month or two keeps the listing looking active.

signals.note: mcneilstree.org is up and clearly lists your services, hours, Lakeside address and phone. Its headings say near Santee, while the shop itself is in Lakeside, and the only way to write to you is a contact form. We also didn't see your contractor license number on the homepage.
signals.next: Mention Lakeside in the main heading alongside Santee, and print your license number near the phone in the footer. A plain email address next to the form gives people who prefer email a second way in.

signals.note: Your street and phone match across your site, Nextdoor and Yelp, which is a good base. Google uses McNeils Tree Service ISA Certified Arborist, Yelp lists the shop as Sean McNeil Tree Service, and your site and Nextdoor say McNeil's Tree Service. Small name splits like that make it harder for search engines to tell the listings are all the same business.
signals.next: Pick one name, most likely McNeil's Tree Service, and use it on Yelp, Nextdoor and Google. Yelp lets the owner request a name edit from the business account.
